title: 2.5 This one, but that one
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Contrast a near thing and a far one with but (This bag is red, but that bag is blue.) and say this one and that one instead of repeating the thing (This one is red, but that one is blue.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.5 This and That: A1 says This is a phone. for a near thing and That is a phone. for a far one; A1+ 2.5 sets the two against each other in one sentence. The one new grammar relationship is but joining two taught clauses (This bag is red, but that bag is blue.), with this one and that one standing for the thing (A1 2.10's Which one? The red one.): This one is red, but that one is blue. Each scene has two photos from the same camera behind the speaker: in the first the speaker looks down at the near thing and touches it (this), in the second the speaker faces the far thing and points down at it (that). A but sentence plays as two turns, so the picture switches on but. Two scenes are also photographed with the colors swapped, so a picture card tells this from that, not the color alone.
prerequisite: A1 2.5 this and that; A1 2.8 colors; A1 2.10 Which one? The red one.; A1 3.12 This car is mine. (this + noun); A1 2.3 bag, chair; A1 2.2 bike; A1+ 1.5 Do you have…?
speaking_outcome: Say but short and weak (/bət/) with a small pause before it; stress the two colors (This one is RED, but that one is BLUE). Say this with a short i and that with an open a. Do not require native-like speed.
